name: Our Lady of Lourdes
note: Marian apparitions to Bernadette Soubirous at the grotto of Massabielle, Lourdes, France, 1858; major healing pilgrimage shrine. Self-identification 'I am the Immaculate Conception.'

name: Our Lady of Fátima
note: Marian apparitions to three shepherd children at Fátima, Portugal, 1917; associated with the 'three secrets' and the Miracle of the Sun.

name: Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal
note: Apparition to Catherine Labouré at the Rue du Bac convent chapel, Paris, 1830; origin of the Miraculous Medal devotion.

name: Our Lady of La Salette
note: Apparition to Maximin Giraud and Mélanie Calvat at La Salette, French Alps, 1846; a weeping Madonna calling for conversion.

name: Our Lady of Knock
note: Silent apparition of Mary, Joseph, John the Evangelist and the Lamb on the Altar at Knock, County Mayo, Ireland, 1879.

name: Our Lady of Beauraing
note: Apparitions ('the Virgin with the Golden Heart') to five children at Beauraing, Belgium, 1932–33; ecclesiastically approved.

name: Our Lady of Banneux
note: Apparitions ('the Virgin of the Poor') to Mariette Beco at Banneux, Belgium, 1933; spring associated with healing.

name: Thérèse of Lisieux
note: Carmelite nun (1873–1897), 'the Little Flower'; Doctor of the Church; author of Story of a Soul; patron of missions.

name: Bernadette Soubirous
note: French peasant girl and later Sister Marie-Bernarde (1844–1879); visionary of the Lourdes apparitions, 1858.

name: John Vianney
note: The Curé d'Ars (1786–1859); model parish priest and confessor; patron saint of parish priests.

name: John Bosco
dom: Education of youth; founder of the Salesians
note: Italian priest (1815–1888); founded the Salesians of Don Bosco; patron of young people and educators.

name: Pio of Pietrelcina
note: Padre Pio (1887–1968), Capuchin friar reported to bear the stigmata; renowned confessor.

name: Faustina Kowalska
note: Polish nun (1905–1938), 'Apostle of Divine Mercy'; her Diary inspired the Divine Mercy devotion and feast.

name: Damien of Molokai
note: Belgian priest (1840–1889) of the Sacred Hearts; served the leper colony of Molokai, Hawaii, and died of leprosy.

name: Frances Xavier Cabrini
note: Italian-American religious (1850–1917), founder of the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart; first U.S. citizen canonized; patron of immigrants.

name: Katharine Drexel
dom: Education; service to Black and Native Americans
note: American heiress and religious (1858–1955); founded the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament for Indians and Colored People.

name: Elizabeth Ann Seton
note: American convert and religious (1774–1821); founder of the Sisters of Charity and the U.S. parochial school system; first native-born U.S. saint.

name: Gemma Galgani
note: Italian mystic (1878–1903), 'the Daughter of Passion'; reported stigmata and ecstasies.

name: Louis Martin
note: French watchmaker (1823–1894), father of Thérèse of Lisieux; canonized 2015 with his wife Zélie.

name: Zélie Martin
note: French lacemaker (1831–1877), mother of Thérèse of Lisieux; canonized 2015 with her husband Louis.

name: Teresa of Calcutta
note: Mother Teresa (1910–1997), Albanian-Indian religious; founder of the Missionaries of Charity. Distinct from the 16th-c. Teresa of Ávila (ENT_EMC_TERESA_AVILA).

name: John Paul II
note: Karol Wojtyła (1920–2005), Polish pope 1978–2005; canonized 2014; promoted the Divine Mercy devotion.

name: John XXIII
note: Angelo Roncalli (1881–1963), 'the Good Pope'; convened the Second Vatican Council; canonized 2014.

name: Edith Stein
note: Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (1891–1942); Jewish-born philosopher and Carmelite nun killed at Auschwitz; martyr and co-patron of Europe.

name: Óscar Romero
note: Archbishop of San Salvador (1917–1980); martyred at the altar; voice for the poor; canonized 2018.

name: Junípero Serra
dom: Mission; founding of the California missions
note: Spanish Franciscan missionary (1713–1784); founded the first California missions; canonized 2015.

name: Gianna Beretta Molla
note: Italian physician and mother (1922–1962); declined treatment to protect her unborn child; canonized 2004; patron of mothers.

name: Pier Giorgio Frassati
note: Italian layman (1901–1925), 'the Man of the Beatitudes'; mountaineer and social activist; beatified 1990.

name: Solanus Casey
note: American Capuchin friar (1870–1957); porter and counselor known for healings; beatified 2017.

name: The Seers of Fátima
note: Collective hub for the three shepherd children who witnessed the Fátima apparitions of 1917: Lúcia, Francisco and Jacinta.

name: Lúcia dos Santos
note: Eldest Fátima seer (1907–2005); later a Carmelite nun (Sister Lúcia); author of the Fátima Memoirs.

name: Francisco Marto
note: Fátima seer (1908–1919); died young; canonized with his sister Jacinta in 2017.

name: Jacinta Marto
note: Youngest Fátima seer (1910–1920); died young; canonized with her brother Francisco in 2017.

name: Modern Marian Apparitions
note: Collective hub grouping the approved modern (1800–present) apparitions of the Virgin Mary.
